newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 GDP up 1.4 pct, budget deficit widens.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 GDP up 1.4 pct, budget deficit widens.

text.p: The German economy grew provisionally at a real 1.4 percent rate in 1996, marginally slower than economists had expected, the German statistics office said on Thursday.

The office also said Germany's 1996 budget deficit, critical for membership in the planned European single currency set to begin in 1999, was 3.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) compared with 3.5 percent of GDP in 1995.
A Reuter poll of economists' forecasts had expected growth for the year at about 1.5 percent amid views that economic growth virtually ground to a halt in the final quarter of 1996.

The economic data for 1997 will be crucial since it will be part of the basis for deciding whether Germany can participate in the currency. The Maastricht Treaty sets as a requirement that the budget deficit may not exceed three percent of GDP.

The office said it expected the German economy to remain weak but that conditions were favourable in 1997. Economic growth during 1996 was mainly driven by exports and capital as well as state spending.

But statistics office officials told a news conference that 1996 growth was only moderate given the favourable economic conditions and that they assumed there was zero growth on a seasonally-adjusted basis in the 1996 fourth quarter.

Economists have said the present cold weather gripping Germany could hamper construction so much that the economy might contract in the first quarter of 1997 -- as it did a year ago -- with little improvement likely before the spring.
